title: Senior's toolkit: doubles and fake time
summary: The NSubstitute calls you use weekly (and their Moq spelling), argument capture, call order, the NSubstitute analyzers, and FakeTimeProvider's controls.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: doubles
steps.body: The handful of calls that cover nearly every mocking need, plus the analyzer that catches the mistakes NSubstitute cannot see at compile time.

toolkit.what: Stub an answer. Several values return one per call; a lambda computes it from the arguments.
flags: first call 1, then 2, then 3 (and 3 after that)

toolkit.what: Verify an outgoing call (a command). Check the arguments that matter with Arg.Is.
Capture an argument to assert on it in detail afterwards (a spy without writing a class).
flags: run code with the argument on each call
every call made, for debugging a failing verify

toolkit.what: Roslyn analyzers for NSubstitute: they flag stubbing a non-virtual member (silently ignored), Received without a call, and argument matchers used outside a call.
flags: substituting for a non-virtual member does nothing
Received() checks nothing without a following call

toolkit.what: Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing: a clock that only moves when the test says so, and fires timers when it does.
flags: move forward, firing due timers and delays
make GetLocalNow independent of the machine
move this much on every GetUtcNow call

steps.prompt: Match the need to the call.
pairs: the first call fails, the retry succeeds
inspect the e-mail body that was sent
the audit entry is written before the payment
a 30-minute session timeout in a unit test
a verify fails and you want to see what was called

steps.prompt: A test stubs `prices.Total(cart).Returns(99m)` on a substitute for a **class** `PriceService`, whose `Total` is not `virtual`. The code under test still gets the real total. What happened?
options: NSubstitute can only intercept virtual (or interface) members; the stub was silently ignored. NSubstitute.Analyzers reports it as NS1000.
The real `Total` was called because the test is async
Substitutes for classes must be strict
steps.explain: Library doubles work by generating a subclass (with Castle.Core) that overrides members. A non-virtual member cannot be overridden, so the real code runs. Substitute interfaces, and add the analyzers so the compiler tells you.

steps.prompt: Verify that exactly one `OrderPlaced` with order id 42 was published.
steps.explain: `Received(1)` counts the calls, `Arg.Is` checks the argument's content, `Arg.Any` ignores the token.
